one_liner: A new PSD covariance estimator lifts a 10-asset tangency portfolio's out-of-sample Sharpe to 0.56 versus 0.51 for Gerber and shrinkage rivals.
Restricted Boltzmann free energy failed to flag the COVID crash on a 19-series cross-asset panel; only the Gaussian variant tracked VIX spikes.
A stochastic-volatility feed into an LSTM cut 21-day S&P 500 volatility forecast error to 5.3% MAPE, but the trading version only reached Sharpe 0.54.
A genetic-algorithm-tuned SVR cut one-year-ahead price forecast error on five global indices by 20% versus LSTM, with no trading test.
Stacking a Bayesian VAR ensemble, Student-t Black-Litterman and a TD3 agent on 29 Dow stocks returned 57% with Sharpe 1.72 over one test window.
An exploratory mean-variance policy under jump diffusion beat the plain calibrated policy on Sharpe in 12 of 14 rolling S&P 500 test years.
Hawkish and dovish LLM macro agents beat a deterministic z-score rule on commodity ETFs by 0.04 Sharpe, and survived costs the rule did not.
An LSTM plus PPO allocator across stocks and crypto reached Sharpe 0.96, but plain PPO without the LSTM scored higher at 1.02.
An LSTM ensembled with Levy jump-diffusion volatility paths hit R-squared 0.997 forecasting Brent and European index price levels.
A Bayesian dynamic linear model beat GARCH-t on S&P 500 VaR coverage but still failed the conditional coverage test; the LSTM passed.
Neural forecasts of the US and euro zero curve hit 56% and 53% directional accuracy, and the duration-managed bond strategy reached Sharpe 1.2.
A graph attention network forecasting 79 FTSE 100 stocks did best with a 5-day window, and correlation graphs beat fundamental-ratio graphs.
Five classic microstructure signal families tested over 34 out-of-sample quarters returned 0.55% a year against SPY's 13.2%, with t-statistic 0.96.
Swapping a point head for a Gaussian mixture head lifted forecast skill more than changing the backbone; classical models still win at short horizons.
A correlation graph attention model on 66 coins reached Sharpe 3.1 after costs, and time-mixing modules that help stocks hurt crypto.
The transformer with the lowest crypto forecast error was not the most profitable; on Ethereum every model finished near zero return.
The 80% directional accuracy claimed for fine-tuned foundation models is just the rising-market base rate; excess accuracy is negative.
Six pretrained time-series foundation models took 8 of 10 return-forecast wins over trained baselines, but none beat a zero-return random walk significantly.
A shifted data augmentation scheme cut Transformer index-level forecast error by two thirds and shrank the spread across ten random seeds.
A streaming neural Hawkes graph over July 2022 news picked next-day extreme movers at 1.5 to 1.8 times the random rate.
LLM-written macro stress scenarios produced VaR and CVaR roughly 3.7 times the historical bootstrap level for a 60/30/10 ETF portfolio.
A network that learns a state-dependent Wasserstein radius returned 26% a year with Sharpe 1.30 on 20 S&P 500 names over one test window.
A physics-informed offline RL policy trading under quadratic impact reached Sharpe 1.49 against 1.07 for equal weight, using a synthetic alpha.
A compact neural minimum-variance model held Sharpe 1.12 at 3x leverage against 0.88 for hierarchical risk parity, and pushed the liquidation threshold higher.
Turning daily LLM regime probabilities into a Belief-at-Risk measure produced spikes at the 2025 tariff shock, roughly ten times the calm baseline.
Feeding 482 LSTM outputs into a random forest raised test AUC from 0.563 to 0.566, a gain well inside the confidence interval.
Forcing a deep asset pricing model to reproduce nine analyst-consensus variables raised out-of-sample R-squared from 7.6% to 10.5% and long-short Sharpe to 1.44.
Randomizing volatility so filtering ambiguity stays stationary improved deep hedging risk on 6 of 10 synthetic payoffs versus a standard learned benchmark.
An LLM regime filter feeding Black-Litterman scored Sharpe 1.68, yet equal weight earned more, and the model's crisis probabilities were badly miscalibrated.
A backtested options wheel on leveraged ETFs reports 15.3% a year with zero assignments across 1,563 puts, including 2008 and 2022.
Across sixteen futures, equal weighting matched an LSTM allocator at zero cost and buried it at 10 basis points; only the transformer held up.
